summary: Hamilton County lookout: a wooden tower from 1911, the steel Aermotor tower of 1919, closed in 1970, restored in 2003 and open to hikers.

facts.design: 35-ft Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7x7 ft metal cab

access.note: Open to hikers since the 2003 restoration; reached on foot by a trail from Endion Road off NY 30

visit.trail_note: 3.2-mile ascent with about 1,200 ft of gain from a trailhead on Endion Road; the trail passes the old observer's cabin foundation and the NHLR reports it is well marked

events.note: First wooden state fire tower, after a 1908 fire destroyed Long Lake West
Payroll roster's first observer starts August 1911
Current steel Aermotor LS-40 tower; replaced the wooden tower
Roster's last observer served April to October 1968; NHLR says staffed until 1970
Closed as airplanes replaced fire observers; roster says not staffed in 1969 and decommissioned in 1970
DEC and Friends of Owl Head Fire Tower restored the lookout; NHLR says it is again open for hikers
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 27, 2006

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower was staffed until 1970. The payroll roster lists the last observer in 1968 and says the tower was not staffed in 1969 and was decommissioned in 1970. Wikipedia dates the closure to 1970. The story reports both readings.

notes_for_editor: Restoration year rests on the NHLR alone (2003). A WebSearch summary mentioned 2004 and a 2005 Friends group, but no fetched page confirmed them, so they are not used. andyarthur.org returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The brief's elevation of 828.1 m matches the NHLR figure (2,717 ft); Wikipedia gives the summit as 2,786 ft (849 m), so elevation was not added to facts. The NHLR visit report carries no date. Roster quotes were checked against the cached PDF text. Observer names are not used in the story.
